Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varphi_i(\mu)>0$; let $B$ be the cogood
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\cup B$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$F_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to $D(\nu)$,
and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $F_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varphi_i(\mu)$
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]).

antipode-invariant, and $D(\mu),D(\nu)$ are simple and self-dual
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]],
[[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]).

In the notation of
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]], let
$B$ be an addable $i$-node of the $p$-restricted partition $\mu$ such that
$\nu=\mu\cup B$ is again $p$-restricted, and let $F_i$ be the residue-summand
induction functor of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]. Then
$$[\,F_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=0$$
if $B$ is not a conormal $i$-node of $\mu$, and
$$[\,F_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=\#\{B':\ B'\ \text{conormal }i\text{-node of }\mu\text{ weakly above }B\}$$
(counting $B$ itself) if $B$ is conormal. The dual Specht-to-induction Hom
criterion (Kleshchev survey Theorem 11.7(i), Brundan 1998 Theorem 2.5 dual
form) is a distinct statement and is not asserted here.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$; let $A$ be the good
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\setminus A$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). For the
residue-summand functor $E_i$ of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]] the
module $E_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to
$D(\nu)$, and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $E_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)$. Thus the Loewy endpoints are simple even though the
formal character of $E_iD(\mu)$ may contain the additional normal-node
factors of
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]].

[F2] $\operatorname{Res}D(\mu)=\bigoplus_jE_jD(\mu)$ is a direct sum of
$kS_{d-1}$-submodules. If $X$ is a removable $i$-node of $\mu$,
$\mu\setminus X$ is $p$-restricted, and $D(\mu\setminus X)$ occurs as a
composition factor of the restriction, then every occurrence belongs to the
summand $E_iD(\mu)$ with $\operatorname{res}(X)=i$
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]); the
localization is proved in
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]].

[F4] $D(\mu)$ is self-dual for $p$-restricted $\mu$, and the functor $E_i$
commutes with contragredient duality, so $E_iD(\mu)$ is self-dual; and
$D(\nu)$ is simple, self-dual and absolutely irreducible
([[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]],

$$[\,E_iD(\mu):D(\nu)\,]=\#\{B:\ B\ \text{normal }i\text{-node of }\mu\text{ weakly below }A\}$$

**The basic module and its lower basis.** Let
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$ be the
transported highest-weight module of the vacuum; by
[[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
its crystal is the $e$-restricted component and its labels are the $e$-restricted
partitions. For an $e$-restricted $\lambda$ define
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) := J^{-1}G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda'),$$
where $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)$ is the lower global (canonical) basis element of
the Fock space at the standard vector $|\mu\rangle$
([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).
Then $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) \equiv M_\lambda \bmod q\,(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$
and the family $\{G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)\}$ is the transported lower global
basis of $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$, indexed by the restricted labels. Define the
**level-one transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention** by the
finite weightwise expansion
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) = \sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\, M_\mu ,$$
the sum being over the partitions $\mu$ of the weight of $\lambda$.

[F1] $F_{\mathrm{QG}}$ carries the lower global basis $\{G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)\}$
of [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]:
an explicit wedge bar $\psi$ with vacuum fixed, $q \mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$U$/bar compatibility; the integral triangular correction
$G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda) = |\lambda\rangle + \sum_{\mu \text{ strictly dominated by } \lambda} d_{\mu\lambda}(q)|\mu\rangle$
with $d_{\mu\lambda} \in q\mathbb{Z}[q]$, diagonal $1$, same $e$-core support and
$G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda) \equiv |\lambda\rangle \bmod qF_0$; the full family is
an $A$-basis of the partition Laurent lattice and an $A_0$ basis, and exactly
the $e$-regular $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda)$ form the lower global basis of
$M_{\mathrm{QG}} = V(\Lambda_0)$; the bar reverses the wedge word and multiplies
by a scalar depending only on the residues of the entries (its unequal-residue
pair count), so it preserves the weight multiset; LT's transpose statement
concerns the bar matrix, not $D$, and the equality
$d_{\lambda\mu} = d_{\mu'\lambda'}$ for all lower coefficients is false.

In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.

[F3] The transition polynomials have off-diagonal entries in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=m$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).
